title: The text discusses the economic measures and budget proposals of Zambia and Nigeria in the early 1990s. Zambia's government proposed a significant increase in expenditure for 1991, focusing on social action programs, education, and defense spending, while also implementing tax changes. In contrast, Nigeria experienced a windfall from rising oil revenues due to the Gulf Crisis, leading to debates on how to effectively utilize the surplus. Suggestions included investing in heavy industries and supporting local oil exploration. However, the government faced pressure from creditors regarding debt repayment, complicating its financial strategies.
